Proves AG-2's `nextQuarter` date preset: AG Grid sends `{ "filterType": "date", "type": "nextQuarter" }` with `dateFrom`/`dateTo` both absent (presets are in AG Grid's own `zeroInputTypes` set), and the adapter — never a compiler — must resolve it into an absolute range. With this category's pinned `requestContext.now` of `2026-08-12T14:37:00Z` and `requestContext.zone` of `UTC`, the current day is 2026-08-12 (a Wednesday), so `nextQuarter` covers the calendar quarter after the current one (Q4 = October-December): the half-open range `[2026-10-01, 2027-01-01)`.

The resolved IR is a single `comparison` node with `op: "inRange"`, `fromInclusive: true`, `toInclusive: false` — read from AG Grid's own published preset spec table (`dateFilterHandler.ts`), which states every preset range as half-open `[from, to)`. This is NOT the "invented inclusivity default" SEM-4 and `spec/fixtures/README.md` forbid asserting for a *native* `inRange` (which carries no inclusivity signal on the wire at all, and is why the adapter rejects it outright): here the value is documented upstream, not guessed. `hireDate` is declared `date` in `schema.json`, so both bounds are `dateValue`s — local calendar dates with no zone and no manufactured instant, per SEM-4.
